citation.title: Components of sensorimotor adaptation in young and elderly subjects

parsed.eligibility_rationale: Upper-extremity visuomotor rotation task comparing age groups, with performance reported during the perturbation and during a no-feedback aftereffect phase: "Twelve young and twelve old subjects executed center-out pointing movements while visual feedback about their fingertip was either veridical (baseline), 60-deg rotated (adaptation), or absent (after-effect)." Written in English.
parsed.design_notes: (1) Repeated exposure: the same experimental young/old subjects who adapted in the pointing task were subsequently transferred to a rotated tracking task ("The experiment concluded with ten transfer episodes of tracking with +60° rotated feedback"); this transfer phase is a repeated/second exposure in the same participants and is not used as an independent adaptation dataset. (2) Contextual change: the pointing aftereffect phase uses the same pointing task as adaptation ("Next came five after-effect episodes of pointing without feedback"), so no contextual change affects the late_adaptation/aftereffect pair; the tracking transfer, by contrast, is a different movement category and is only a transfer measure, with the rotation still applied (not an aftereffect). (3) Multiple rounds: a "refresh" phase of three rotated pointing episodes followed the aftereffect phase after a five-minute break; only the initial 15-episode adaptation round is used. (4) Separate control samples (young and old) performed tracking only and were never exposed to pointing adaptation ("we recruited additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age) healthy and naïve volunteers. Those subjects only executed ten tracking episodes with veridical feedback on the first day and five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback on the second day"). (5) N discrepancy: the text states 12 per group (48 total), yet the transfer ANOVA reports "F(1,43)=144,09", whose error df suggests 47 rather than 48 analysed subjects; the paper never explains this, so 12 per group (the stated analysed n) is reported. (6) All group means for adaptation/aftereffect appear only in Fig. 1 (means ± SD plotted); the text reports only exponential fits and ANOVA statistics, no tabulated adaptation or aftereffect values.

datasets.chosen_pair_rationale: The experimental young and older pointing groups are the only pair exposed to the visuomotor rotation in a pointing task with both an adaptation phase and a no-feedback after-effect phase; the tracking-only control groups (young control, old control) were not chosen for this dataset because they never performed the perturbed pointing task, and the pooled 54-senior sample is not an age contrast.
datasets.notes: Late adaptation would come from the end of the 15 adaptation episodes and the aftereffect from the five no-feedback pointing episodes; both are plotted only in Fig. 1 (means with SD). Text gives exponential fits ("y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young subjects and y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old subjects") and ANOVA results, but no printed group means. Dropped from this dataset: refresh phase (second exposure to rotation) and the tracking transfer phase (different movement category, rotation still present).
